newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium on brink during LME evening trading.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium on brink during LME evening trading.

text.p: Aluminium prices slid back during Tuesday evening inter-office LME trading, as the market headed back towards a test of the $1,454 a tonne 23-month lows notched up in mid-July.

Traders said the market's early tumble under speculative selling knocked away the prop of expected consumer buying, and with LME warehouse stocks rising by 4,700 tonnes prices look likely to remain on the defensive.
A fall in IPAI producer inventories in July was shrugged off, as being historic.
"That (the IPAI fall) was what happened then. This (the LME increase) is happening now and looks like continuing," one trader said.
Also, this week's major aluminium industry conference in Germany has generated little in the way of obvious bullish developments, traders said.
At 1800 gmt three months aluminium prices were indicated at $1,458/62 a tonne, against a $1,462 kerb close, and down from Monday's $1,477 finish.
Below $1,454, the next chart objective is around $1,420/25, they added.
Copper prices held relatively steady this evening, but are seen testing support at $1,905/10 in the short-term. Three months settled at $1,923/28 a tonne, little changed from Monday.
